listing.name: Multi-Model Coordination
listing.summary: Decide who produces, who reviews, and when a review actually counts across two or more models - plan gate, version-locked envelopes, independent review, evidence-gated delivery.
listing.description:
Two or more models, one deliverable. This skill fixes the parts that quietly fail: who owns the work, what a hand-off must contain, when a review is trustworthy, and how to stop without degrading.

**What it gives your agent**

- Roles with hard boundaries: lead, planner, producer, reviewer, dispatcher. One owner per artifact, and a producer never signs off its own work.
- A 12-rule contract that survives model switches: no envelope, no review; schema before adoption; reviewer writes nothing; independence is a property of the model pair, not the prompt.
- A plan gate: the planner restates the requirement, compares at least two approaches, names a stack and a work-package table, and a different model family reviews the plan before anything is produced.
- Version-locked review: artifact hash plus modification time in every envelope; a reviewer that saw an older file is discarded, not argued with.
- Evidence gates: test command, exit code, log hash and a verbatim excerpt travel with the review; a review with no behavioural evidence is static-only and must say so.
- Budgets and stop lines: two review rounds per milestone by default, a written reason for a third, and a hard stop instead of a silent retry loop.
- Safe version iteration: stable drives candidate, baseline comparison, human approval of the exact commit, promotion with a rollback that does not depend on the candidate.
- Routing and failure triage for rate limits, quota, proxies, stale context and model swaps.

**Includes** the protocol skill plus two reference files: `references/envelopes.md` (request and result shapes, adoption procedure, common failure modes) and `references/checklists.md` (pre-flight, plan, dispatch, review, delivery and failure-triage checklists you can copy).

**Who it is for** developers and teams already calling more than one model - GPT plus Claude, DeepSeek plus Qwen, or a lead agent with subagents - who need the output to be reviewable instead of a pile of merged opinions.

**Free and open source.** The portable protocol is what you get here. The full reference implementation - model registry, routing, review budgets, plan gate, iteration and promotion, as a DeepSeek Harness plugin - is MIT-licensed at https://github.com/zlzyangreal/coordination_of_multiple_large_models

No install, no API key of its own, no network calls from the skill: it changes how your agent already uses the models it has.
use_cases: Split a feature across a planner model, a producer model and an independent reviewer
Stop a model from approving its own output
Decide which model to use when one is rate-limited, out of quota or timing out
Run a plan review before any code is written
Reject a review that was written against an older version of the file
Hand a task to a subagent without losing the acceptance criteria
listing.requirement_note: Works with any agent that can call two or more models, directly or through subagents. Nothing to install.

file_scopes: project files under the working directory
permissions.notes: The skill only instructs your agent. It makes no network calls of its own; model calls are the ones your agent already makes.

listing.sample_input: Plan and build the retry logic in src/fetcher.ts. Use one model to produce it and a different family to review it. I only want it delivered if the tests pass.
listing.sample_output: A plan with two approaches and a work-package table, a plan review from a different model family, one producer run on src/fetcher.ts, an independent review with findings verified at source, the test command and exit code recorded in the envelope, and a delivery summary that states which findings were accepted, rejected or deferred.
